source_text: Μετὰ ταῦτά. φησι πρὸς ἡμᾶς δῆθεν (ἵνα τηρήσω τὸ ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς τῷ Ἰουδαίῳ προτεθὲν) ὁ τοῦ Κέλσου Ἰουδαῖος ἐν τῷ πρὸς τοὺς πολίτας ἑαυτοῦ λόγῳ πιστεύσαντας· τίνι οὖν προσήχθητε ἢ διότι προεῖπεν, ὡς ἀποθανὼν ἀναστήσεται; καὶ τοῦτο δ᾿ εἰς τὸ περὶ Μωϋσέως ὁμοίως τοῖς προτέροις κοινοποιηθήσεται. φήσομεν γὰρ πρὸς αὐτόν· τίνι οὖν προσήχθητε ἢ διότι ἀνέγραψε περὶ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ τελευτῆς τοιαῦτα· „καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν ἐκεῖ Μωϋσῆς οἰκέτης κυρίου ἐν γῇ Μωὰβ διὰ ῥήματος κυρίου· καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτὸν ἐν γῇ Μωάβ, ἐγγὺς οἴκου Φογώρ. Καὶ οὐδεὶς οἶδε τὴν ταφὴν αὐτοῦ ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης" Ὡς γὰρ διαβάλλει ὁ Ἰουδαῖος ὅτι προεῖπεν, ὡς ἀποθανὼν ἀναστήσεται, πρὸς τὸν λέγοντα ταῦτα ὁ περὶ Μωϋσέως τὸ ὅμοιον φάσκων ἐρεῖ ὅτι [καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἀνέγραψενμδαση;αὐτοῦ γάρ ἐστι καὶ τὸ Δευτερονόμιον] ὅτι θυοτ;Οὐδεὶς οἶδε τὴν ταφὴν αὐτοῦ ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης," σεμνύνων καὶ ἐπαίρων καὶ τὴν ταφὴν αὐτοῦ ὡς οὐκ ἐγνωσμένην ἀνθρώπων γένει.
pass_a_gloss: After these he says to us, supposedly (δῆθεν) (so that I may keep (τηρέω) what was set before (προτίθημι) the Jew from the beginning), Celsus's Jew in the speech (λόγος) to his own fellow citizens (πολῖται) who believed: 'to what then were you drawn (προσάγω, aor. pass.), or because he foretold (προλέγω) that having died (ἀποθνῄσκω) he will rise (ἀνίστημι)?' And this too will be made common (κοινοποιέω) to the matter about Moses like the former things. For we shall say to him: 'to what then were you drawn, or because he wrote up (ἀναγράφω) such things about his own end (τελευτή): and Moses the household servant (οἰκέτης) of the Lord (κύριος) died there in the land of Moab through the word (ῥῆμα) of the Lord; and they buried (θάπτω) him in the land of Moab near the house of Phogor (οἶκος Φογώρ). And no one knows his burial (ταφή) until this day.' For as the Jew slanders (διαβάλλω) that he foretold that having died he will rise, to the one saying these things the one asserting the like (ὅμοιον) about Moses will say that [Moses too wrote; for Deuteronomy (Δευτερονόμιον) is also his] that 'no one knows his burial until this day', dignifying (σεμνύνω) and exalting (ἐπαίρω) also his burial as not known (γιγνώσκω) to the race (γένος) of men.
pass_b_english: After this the Jew of Celsus, in his speech to those of his own people who have believed, says, as if to us (to keep to the part assigned to the Jew from the start): “What, then, drew you to him, unless it was that he foretold that after dying he would rise again?” (compare Matthew 16:21). This too, like what came before, will be turned against Moses in the same way. For we shall say to him: ‘What, then, drew you to him, unless it was that he wrote such things about his own death: “And Moses, the servant of the Lord, died there in the land of Moab, by the word of the Lord; and they buried him in the land of Moab, near the house of Phogor. And no one knows his burial to this day” (Deuteronomy 34:5–6)?’

For just as the Jew makes it a charge that Jesus foretold that after dying he would rise again, so the man who argues the like about Moses will reply to the one who says this that Moses too wrote (for Deuteronomy also is his) that “no one knows his burial to this day” (Deuteronomy 34:6), dignifying and exalting even his burial as unknown to the human race.

choices.why: ἵνα τηρήσω: '(for I keep to...)' -> '(to keep to...)', restoring the purpose clause
διαβάλλει: 'sneers that' -> 'makes it a charge that'
added inline (Deuteronomy 34:6) to the repeated quotation
Deuteronomy 34:5-6 checked against LXX (οἰκέτης, οἴκου Φογώρ); Matthew 16:21 confirmed

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; English is from the Greek.

notes: Translated from the Greek of the staged Koetschau row only; Crombie (ANF) and Chadwick were not used.

translator_notes: The staged Greek is corrupt in the bracketed clause: ‘ἀνέγραψενμδαση;αὐτοῦ’ and ‘ὅτι θυοτ;Οὐδεὶς’ contain stray characters (likely encoding debris for brackets and quotation marks). Read as [καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἀνέγραψεν· αὐτοῦ γάρ ἐστι καὶ τὸ Δευτερονόμιον] ὅτι ‘Οὐδεὶς οἶδε...’; the bracketed words (Koetschau’s square brackets, a suspected insertion) are translated as a parenthesis. ἢ διότι in Celsus’s question rendered ‘unless it was that’. δῆθεν and the parenthesis mean Origen answers ‘as if to us’ while keeping Celsus’s frame of a Jew addressing Jewish believers. Jesus’ foretelling of his resurrection (Matthew 16:21; Mark 8:31) is cited as ‘compare’ since Celsus paraphrases. Deuteronomy 34:5–6 is quoted from the LXX: ‘servant’ renders οἰκέτης; ‘near the house of Phogor’ keeps the LXX form of Beth-peor. Verse numbers agree in LXX and English.
